title: Making male friends
reason: 昨天的课程讨论休息、创造力和数字刺激，今天轮换到日常人际关系。本集探讨成年男性维系友谊时面临的困难、朋友在困难时期的支持作用，以及社交媒体和线下社交空间的影响。内容适合周末学习，也能自然迁移到同事关系和团队支持。练习会反复调用六个高频表达，从原文回忆逐步过渡到受控改写和有限个人表达。

targetExpressions.meaning: experience and talk about both the good and difficult parts of life with someone
targetExpressions.usage: Use it for a supportive relationship: Close friends share life's ups and downs instead of meeting only when things are going well.

targetExpressions.meaning: keep close relationships healthy and active over time
targetExpressions.usage: Use maintain with a relationship that needs continuing effort: Regular contact helps people maintain strong friendships.

targetExpressions.meaning: during periods of trouble, unhappiness or financial difficulty
targetExpressions.usage: Use it to introduce support needed in difficult periods: Good teammates help each other when times are tough.

targetExpressions.meaning: manage to live through or deal with a difficult situation
targetExpressions.usage: Use get through + a problem or period: Her friends helped her get through a stressful month.

targetExpressions.meaning: gradually become less close until a relationship weakens or ends
targetExpressions.usage: Use it when distance grows slowly without one clear break: Old friends can drift away when nobody stays in contact.

targetExpressions.meaning: something that has both favourable and unfavourable consequences
targetExpressions.usage: Use it to present two sides of one thing: Remote work can be a double-edged sword for team relationships.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the opening idea: “Everyone needs friends to ______.”
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Beth says everyone needs friends to share life's ups and downs, meaning both positive and difficult experiences.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the programme's observation: “Men may find it harder to ______, especially as they get older.”
objectiveQuestions.explanation: The transcript directly says men may find it harder to maintain strong friendships as they get older.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete Claudia Hammond's point: “______, friends are often the people who listen, reassure us and offer advice.”
objectiveQuestions.explanation: The phrase introduces periods of trouble or difficulty when support from friends is especially valuable.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: What does “get through” mean in the discussion of friendship?

options.text: Successfully manage to live through an unpleasant period
End a friendship immediately after an argument
Contact every person in a social network
Pretend that a difficult situation does not exist

objectiveQuestions.explanation: The programme defines get through as managing to live through a difficult situation; friends can provide the support that helps.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Which situation best illustrates two friends “drifting away”?

options.text: They gradually contact each other less until the connection becomes weak.
They have one disagreement and formally end the friendship that day.
They meet more often after moving to different cities.
They plan a regular activity to keep the relationship active.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: Drift away describes a gradual movement apart, not a sudden decision to end the relationship.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete Max's description of publicly representing a book called Billy No-Mates: “It is ______.”
objectiveQuestions.explanation: The book title is memorable and can raise awareness, but it also publicly labels Max as a person without friends, so it has favourable and unfavourable consequences.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Why can social media make loneliness feel worse according to the episode?

options.text: It can create the impression that everyone else is enjoying time with friends.
It proves that online users have no friends in real life.
It prevents all younger people from joining clubs.
It makes people automatically maintain strong friendships.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: The transcript says social media can make it seem as though everyone is having a great time with their mates except you, which may intensify loneliness.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Which sentence uses the target expression naturally in a work context?

options.text: Occasional messages and honest conversations can help former colleagues maintain strong friendships.
The server maintained strong friendships after the restart.
We maintained strong friendships the deadline yesterday.
A strong friendship maintained the database automatically.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: Maintain strong friendships describes people making continuing efforts to keep close relationships healthy; the other choices misuse the expression.

assessment.retellingPrompt: Without looking at the full transcript, retell the episode in 80–120 words using this structure: (1) topic—why close friendship matters; (2) two key ideas—how friendships can drift away and why loneliness may be difficult to recognise; (3) response—how people can build or maintain connections. Phrase bank: “when times are tough”, “drift away”, “a double-edged sword”. Use at least two phrases naturally. Simple, accurate sentences are enough.
referencePoints: Close friends help people share life's ups and downs and support mental wellbeing.
Friends may listen, reassure or advise people when times are tough and help them get through difficult periods.
The programme considers the stereotype that women maintain friendships more actively while men may simply spend time with whoever is nearby.
Relationships can drift away gradually when they are not nurtured.
Max Dickins is young, generous and outgoing, showing that loneliness does not always match common expectations and increasingly affects younger people.
Social media may intensify loneliness, while third spaces such as sports clubs and reading groups can provide opportunities to meet people.
